requirements.requirement: Create a certificate authority named 'Fleet Internal CA' on node1
requirements.summary: cmd-0a6ef5f8a6644b8e shows a self-signed x509 CA generated on node1 with subject/issuer CN=Fleet Internal CA, O=Fleet Internal CA, basicConstraints CA:true, validity 2026-2036.

requirements.requirement: Issue node2 a TLS certificate signed by the CA
requirements.summary: cmd-68b4af524b0547d7 shows a CSR for node2 (CN=node2, SAN DNS:node2/IP:10.100.105.11, EKU serverAuth) signed by the CA key; cmd-0a4d3158aa184c25 and cmd-2d3840cd5a9442d7 confirm openssl verify OK against the system trust store on both nodes.

requirements.requirement: Configure node2 to serve HTTPS on port 8443 using the issued certificate
requirements.summary: nginx site 'fleet-tls' on node2 (cmd-26b7cf72ced644aa) configures listen 8443 ssl with the issued cert/key; nginx reported active; cmd-c4b697e01a0b488a and cmd-46024a2aa4ed4a53 show curl against https://10.100.105.11:8443 and https://node2:8443 returning HTTP 200 and presenting CN=node2 issued by Fleet Internal CA. The after_executor lifecycle snapshot independently confirms nginx listening on 0.0.0.0:8443 and [::]:8443 on node2, corroborating the config took effect outside the executor's own narrative.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA as a trusted system CA on node1
requirements.summary: cmd-0a4d3158aa184c25 shows the CA cert copied to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates and update-ca-certificates run ('1 added, 0 removed'), with openssl verify against /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt returning OK on node1.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA as a trusted system CA on node2
requirements.summary: cmd-2d3840cd5a9442d7 shows the same CA install process performed on node2, with openssl verify against the system trust store returning OK; subsequent curl invocations without -k (cmd-46024a2aa4ed4a53, cmd-bd7fd09f46b342d5) confirm the system trust store, not an ad hoc CA file, is what validates the chain.

requirements.requirement: (Independent protocol) Provider-wide node-restart evidence: pre-restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/trust state on both nodes
requirements.summary: Both nodes show a full bounded transition: pre-restart baseline with boot_id and healthy trust/service state (cmd-6f25ae667eba4196, cmd-cd60b406cb5a47f2), an acknowledged background reboot (cmd-f0bba40495504c31, cmd-da5af50e7e6d443e), an intermediate connection timeout during the reboot window (cmd-c531dec9e97c4a62, cmd-ab68d741daf94b2d), a new boot_id after reconnection (cmd-c3b6ff6c454b4a27, cmd-5e5394a4bec44a84), and recovered state — CA trust and cross-node HTTPS on node1 (cmd-63b336d536a74498), nginx active plus HTTPS verify-ok on node2 (cmd-5b7416b0fcc04c2b), and a final cross-node HTTPS check (cmd-7e9914ee351f4e6c). The fixed after_executor lifecycle snapshot independently corroborates the final boot IDs and shows nginx listening on 8443/80 with no failed services or package-health issues.

overall_summary: All five material outcomes of the task contract — CA creation on node1, cert issuance for node2, node2 serving HTTPS on 8443 with that cert, and CA trust installation on both nodes — are directly and consistently satisfied by captured command output and cross-checked by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The independent node-restart protocol is also fully and coherently demonstrated on both nodes with matching pre/post boot identities and recovered service/trust state. The only notable gap is minor hygiene residue: an abandoned SSH key/known_hosts artifact left on node1 after a failed transfer attempt, and non-idempotent /etc/hosts appends, neither of which affects task functionality or security posture.
limitations: No independent verification that the SSH private key file left at ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 on node1 was ever removed; its presence is inferred from the absence of any cleanup command in the timeline.

The connection-timeout entries during each reboot window (cmd-c531dec9e97c4a62, cmd-ab68d741daf94b2d) are read as evidence of an actual reboot in progress rather than an unrelated transient network issue; reasonable given the surrounding boot_id change but not itself direct proof of reboot causation.

Only nginx's own HTTP (non-8443) listener and dpkg package-health were checked in the fixed snapshots; no deeper content/data-integrity check (e.g., of the nginx document root) was requested or needed by this task.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor commands were either directly purposeful (CA/cert generation, nginx config, CA trust install) or bounded and fully reverted (the temporary python3 http.server used to transfer cert material, started at cmd-a5311f5fe69141fc and killed at cmd-eed02e00a7154646/cmd-9dcaac6b011545fc). However, an abandoned SSH-based transfer attempt (cmd-90d8d0468d284950) wrote a private key to ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 and populated known_hosts on node1; when that path failed (node2 had no sshd, confirmed by cmd-031794140c6a4537 and the connection-refused in cmd-35b85f6c7bcc4d71), the executor pivoted to the HTTP-server transfer but never removed the now-unused key material — residue from a troubleshooting experiment that did not contribute to the final solution. The /etc/hosts edits (cmd-35b85f6c7bcc4d71, cmd-7275a7d35e23414b, cmd-63b336d536a74498, cmd-5b7416b0fcc04c2b) were necessary for cross-node name resolution but were appended repeatedly without consistent idempotency checks, risking duplicate lines; low severity since it is low-risk and content-only. No failed services, no damaged package state, and no weakened security controls were observed in the after_executor snapshot.
